paper.title: Instruct2Act: Mapping Multi-modality Instructions to Robotic Actions with Large Language Model
paper.central_claim: Instruct2Act uses an LLM to generate Python programs that call SAM/CLIP and robot primitives to map multi-modality instructions to actions, and this zero-shot approach outperforms many learning-based policies in several tasks (comparable average to VIMA on VIMABench).

scope.note: LLM + perception tools + frozen primitives controlling a tabletop arm in simulation: inside EH Radar (A type).

evidence.quote: Instruct2Act employs the LLM model to generate Python programs that constitute a comprehensive perception, planning, and action loop for robotic tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Central operation: LLM emits a Python program that closes perception-planning-action.

evidence.quote: our zero-shot method outperformed many state-of-the-art learning-based policies in several tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Author headline claim (zero-shot vs learned policies), scope 'several tasks'.

evidence.quote: it is restricted to what the perception APIs can provide and struggle to interpret longer and more complex commands due to the high precision requirements of the code
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated limitation of the nearest neighbour Code-as-Policies (CaP); asserted, not tested in the paper.

evidence.quote: final input is a sequence of code APIs, usage examples, and task instructions
evidence.support_explanation: No fine-tuning; the interface is a prompt of API definitions + in-context examples.

evidence.quote: we provide full-logical code examples invoking different modules
evidence.support_explanation: Examples are whole programs for each task family, not only function-level usage.

evidence.quote: we design a prompt that provides coverage for all tasks and has fewer in-context examples
evidence.support_explanation: Prompt examples cover all evaluated task families: development/evaluation overlap at task level.

evidence.quote: SAM outputs masks for all potential objects in the input image, based on which object crops
evidence.support_explanation: Perception path: SAM masks -> crops -> CLIP features.

evidence.quote: we apply a gray threshold filter followed by a morphological closing operation to fill up small holes before sending the image to the SAM
evidence.support_explanation: Hand-built image pre-processing inserted between the foundation model and the downstream task.

evidence.quote: We design a unified retrieval system that utilizes different types of queries to ensure the use of a unified architecture for both types of inputs
evidence.support_explanation: Text/image/pointing queries all resolved by one CLIP-similarity retrieval over mask crops.

evidence.quote: Task success rates were evaluated on 150 instances for each of the six meta-tasks, with three random seeds selected per meta-task to obtain average success rates
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation denominator: 150 instances x 6 meta-tasks, 3 seeds, mean only.

evidence.quote: The VIMABench simulator determined task success if the final states matched the configurations outlined in the instructions
evidence.support_explanation: Success is judged by simulator state (environment truth), not by a learned judge.

evidence.quote: we directly used the experiment results of different baselines from [ 15 ]
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines are copied from the VIMA paper, not re-run by the authors; no CaP baseline appears.
L1 per-task results: equal average (84.4) to VIMA-20M; lower on tasks 01-04, higher on 05 and 17.

evidence.quote: for tasks that require multiple steps to complete, such as Task 05 and Task 17, our Instruct2Act outperforms the previous SOTA by a significant margin
evidence.support_explanation: Author reading of the Table 1 contrast.

evidence.quote: The results from (a-c) show that our method consistently achieved positive results across all levels and various tasks
evidence.support_explanation: L2/L3 generalization claim; numbers are only in Fig 5 (image), so only the author's sentence is readable.

evidence.quote: Mask post-processing directly boosts the success rate to 83.0
evidence.support_explanation: Ablation of processing modules: mask post-processing dominates (51.0 -> 83.0).
Row with no processing modules: average 51.0 across 3 levels.
Row with both processing modules: average 84.1 across 3 levels.

evidence.quote: using only image pre-processing leads to no improvement in performance and may even cause degradation in some tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Component-level toggle shows image pre-processing alone does not help.

evidence.quote: Task 01 Direct More Trail Naive Filtering SR(%) 72.5 77.5 85.5
evidence.support_explanation: Second (open-source) LLM only on Task 01, 40 instances; error-triggered regeneration helps.

evidence.quote: the Python Interpreter can detect these errors and inform us to generate new code
evidence.support_explanation: Only automatic feedback: interpreter exceptions trigger regeneration; no task-level verifier.
SAM backbone ablation with parameter counts (the only cost-like figure).

evidence.quote: A notable drawback of Instruct2Act is its high computational cost, as it employs several foundation models to accomplish robotic tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Cost acknowledged qualitatively, not measured.

evidence.quote: we have only tested our method in a simulation environment so far
evidence.support_explanation: No real-robot evidence.

evidence.quote: Code generation was performed using ChatGPT with the text-davinci-003 engine
evidence.support_explanation: Headline LLM is a single closed API model; contamination/dev overlap not discussed.

evidence.quote: Pointing-Language Enhanced Instruction 90.7 98.0
evidence.support_explanation: Pointing mode evaluated on Task 01/03 with one seed.

evidence.quote: our method is presently limited by the basic action primitives provided in the chosen VIMABench, such as Pick and Place
evidence.support_explanation: Action space is two suction pick/place primitives; no contact-rich control.

signatures.object: LLM-written Python program main() composed of perception APIs (SAM, ImageCrop, CLIPRetrieval, Pixel2Loc) and action APIs (PickPlace, RearrangeActions, DistractorActions) executed by RobotExecution
signatures.information: top-view RGB image, text or multimodal instruction (image crops cached in environment cache C), API definitions + 5 full-program in-context examples + BOUNDS; no simulator state for the agent; no training or fine-tuning
signatures.operation: LLM maps instruction to an executable program that calls foundation-model APIs and primitives
signatures.output: pick/place action list sent to the low-level controller
signatures.conditions: calibrated image-to-robot transform, boundary clamping, two suction primitives, tabletop scenes
signatures.feedback: interpreter exceptions only (regenerate); no task-level success feedback inside an episode
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: none: single program per instruction; error-triggered regeneration used in the LLaMA-Adapter experiment
signatures.persistence: environment cache C holds image crops and coordinate transforms within an episode; nothing persists across tasks
signatures.claimed_effect: VIMABench L1 average 84.4% equals VIMA-20M; better on multi-step Task 05 and Task 17
signatures.failure_boundary: high compute, only pick/place, simulation only; contact feedback absent

signatures.object: pre/post-processing modules wrapped around zero-shot SAM output
signatures.information: raw top-view image and SAM masks
signatures.operation: gray-threshold + closing before SAM; size filter, opening and NMS after SAM
signatures.conditions: tabletop with cast shadows, hand-set thresholds ('pre-defined parameters ... lack tuning')
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: hand-chosen parameters, tuning data not stated
signatures.failure_boundary: image pre-processing alone gives no gain; parameters suboptimal by the authors' own account

signatures.object: modality manager mapping pure-language, language-visual and pointing instructions to one CLIP retrieval
signatures.information: instruction text or image crops/scene images, cursor clicks (pointing mode)
signatures.operation: embed query with CLIP text or image encoder, match against mask-crop features; Hungarian matching for scene-level goals
signatures.output: selected object indices passed to PickPlace

signatures.claimed_effect: multi-modal prompts generally outperform single-modal prompts

gap.author_gap: CaP-style policy code is restricted by the perception APIs and struggles with long/complex commands; no general system covers multi-modality instructions without training.
gap.checked_gap: The CaP limitation is asserted, but no CaP (or any LLM-code) baseline is run; the only baselines are trained policies copied from VIMA. What is verified is that an LLM+SAM+CLIP program can reach the VIMA-20M average on six VIMABench tasks.
lineage: Code as Policies / VISPROG / ViperGPT (LLM writes programs over APIs) -> Instruct2Act (robot-hierarchy API prompt, SAM+CLIP perception, multimodal retrieval, processing modules)
CLIPort / Perceiver-Actor / VIMA (trained instruction-conditioned manipulation policies) = the compared class

closest_adjacent.name: Code as Policies (CaP)
closest_adjacent.solved: LLM writes robot policy code from in-context examples
closest_adjacent.unsolved_per_authors: limited by perception APIs, long complex commands

gap.residue: Whether LLM-composed programs beat other LLM-code harnesses, and how much of the success comes from the hand-tailored prompt examples and processing modules versus the LLM, is not separated.
gap.stakes: Training-free language/vision-conditioned manipulation; foundation-model upgrades could transfer for free.
gap.method_response: Provide a robot-hierarchy API prompt with whole-program examples, bolt on perception post-processing, and route all instruction modalities through CLIP retrieval.
gap.remaining_gap: Compute cost, only pick/place primitives, simulation only (authors); no CaP comparison, no real robot, no seed variance (ours).
gap.unresolved: Neighbour papers (CaP, VISPROG, VIMA) are not pinned in the batch materials, so lineage rests on this paper's own citations; empty retrieval does not prove novelty.

claims.text: An LLM that writes Python programs over SAM/CLIP/pick-place APIs achieves training-free multimodal-instruction manipulation competitive with learned policies.
claims.setting: VIMABench (PyBullet), 6 meta-tasks, L1; text-davinci-003; SAM-H + CLIP-H
claims.baseline_control: DT-20M, Gato-20M, Flamingo-20M, VIMA-20M numbers copied from VIMA paper; no LLM-code baseline
claims.selection_vs_test: prompt examples cover all six evaluated task families; no separate selection split
claims.result_denominator: 150 instances x 3 seeds per meta-task; L1 average 84.4 vs 84.4 (VIMA); task-wise 91.3/81.4/98.2/78.5/72.0/85.2
claims.allowed_conclusion: On six VIMABench L1 tasks the program-writing harness matches VIMA-20M's average (lower on 4 tasks, higher on 2); superiority over learned policies is not established.

claims.text: Processing modules make zero-shot SAM usable for grasping.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Mask post-processing carries almost all of the perception gain; image pre-processing alone does nothing.

claims.text: The approach generalizes to L2 (combinatorial) and L3 (novel object) levels with small fluctuation.
claims.result_denominator: numbers only in Fig 5 (image); text asserts 'positive results across all levels'
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported only; cannot be audited from the fixed text.

claims.text: General-purpose, flexible system usable with open-source LLMs and human intervention.
claims.setting: Task 01 with LLaMA-Adapter (40 instances); qualitative prompts
claims.allowed_conclusion: Anecdotal for flexibility; no evidence of a general-purpose system beyond pick/place tabletop simulation.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: closed-loop simulator-judged success with counts; harness developed on the evaluated task families, no new embodiment/simulator, no real robot -> not transfer (EVIDENCE rule 2)
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On six VIMABench L1 tasks (PyBullet) an LLM program harness over SAM/CLIP/pick-place reaches the same 84.4% average as the trained VIMA-20M (baseline numbers copied), with mask post-processing worth +32 points; superiority, L2/L3 retention, generality and low cost are not established.
assessment.author_claim_kept: Instruct2Act zero-shot outperforms many learning-based policies and is a general-purpose, flexible robotic system.
assessment.retention: not_applicable: static harness, no selection or persistence claim
unresolved: L2/L3 per-task numbers exist only in Fig 5

G.reason: Real, sourced limitation of CaP (perception-API bound, complex commands) and a clear target (training-free multimodal manipulation), but the limitation is never tested against CaP, neighbours are cited not compared, and the residual is stated only as compute/primitive limits.

M.reason: Concrete, reconstructible mechanism with causal story for the perception failures (shadows, holes, duplicates) and an ablation that matches it; the central 'decision-making actions reduce error rate versus CaP' prediction is not tested and prompt examples nearly template the program.

X.reason: Prompt, APIs, processing steps, pointing mode and retrieval are specified (App A.1-A.3) and the chain is rebuildable; thresholds/hyper-parameters of the processing modules, the share of code failures and per-task prompt use are not given, and there is no failure or hand-back handling.

measurement.reason: Closed-loop simulator-judged success with 150 instances x 3 seeds per task and per-task numbers (Table 1) for six tasks, equal-average parity with VIMA; but only L1 numbers are readable (L2/L3 in figure), single-modal results partial, baselines copied, no real run.

causality.reason: Relevant toggles exist for processing modules and SAM/CLIP size, but the key controls are missing: no CaP/other LLM-code harness, no LLM-free fixed-template program, and prompt examples cover every evaluated task, leaving 'prompt+SAM+CLIP template' as a strong alternative explanation.

holdout.reason: Evaluated levels L2/L3 are held-out placements/objects per the author, but the prompt was built to cover the same task families, L4 novel task is excluded, contamination is undiscussed and the L2/L3 figures cannot be audited.

statistics.reason: Three seeds and 150 instances per task support the means, but no variance/CI, no paired statistics and no failure breakdown are reported; LLM-variant experiment is 40 instances single run.

cost.reason: Cost is only acknowledged ('high computational cost'); no calls, tokens, latency or GPU-hours; VIMA parameter count listed but not comparable; no matched-budget comparison.

status_reason: Full text read including appendix; all eight items judged from fixed material; unreadable figure-only numbers kept as unresolved, not scored.
